summary.name: TestDriver
summary.one_liner: TestDriver is an AI code reviewer and end-to-end testing tool that runs each pull request in a real desktop sandbox, finds bugs, and generates regression tests.
use_cases: Automatically test every pull request in a GitHub repo
Generate end-to-end regression tests from PR changes
Test desktop apps (Windows, macOS, Electron, Tauri, Qt) without selectors
Run UI tests unattended in CI pipelines
Test browser extensions or VS Code extensions end-to-end
Track test pass rates and flaky tests across runs
summary.what_it_does: TestDriver reads a pull request diff with an AI vision agent, then runs the application in a real desktop sandbox and tests it by clicking, typing, and reading the screen rather than using selectors or the DOM. Once a test passes, it opens a new PR containing the generated test code, written in Vitest. Tests can self-heal by re-invoking the AI to locate elements when the UI changes, and failing runs can be replayed as video with network logs and click history. The platform also tracks pass rates, flaky tests, and failure trends, and exports results as JUnit XML.
notable: Runs each pull request in a real desktop sandbox and generates tests from the PR content
Self-healing element lookup that updates cached elements when the UI changes
Contributes generated tests back as a new pull request
Tests are plain Vitest and export JUnit XML
caveats: Cloud Pro plan is $20 per seat per month and includes 120 testing minutes; extra minutes cost $0.14 each
Seats are billed for every GitHub user who gets a PR review or runs a test
Self-hosted Enterprise tier is custom-priced and requires contacting sales
